summary: Chun-fang Yu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University (~1968–1973) and under Nanting and Sheng Yen. She held posts at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and as Professor at Columbia University (attested 2007–2015).

Chun-min Yen specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yen earned a PhD at the University of Arizona (attested 2004) under Robert M. Gimello, also studying under Todd Brown, Chanyun, and Sheng Yen.

Chögyam Trungpa (1939–1987) was a figure in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at St Antony's College, University of Oxford (~1963–1967), and with multiple teachers including Khenpo Gangshar and Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drime. He founded Naropa University in 1973.
Chönyi Drolma works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Drolma studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (all attested 2011).
Clare Carlisle works in philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1995–2002), and served as Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011).

Claude Jacques (1929–2018) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under George Cœdès (~1960–1969). He served as director at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1963–1973) and taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2017).
Claudia Weber works in Indology and religious studies. She studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and project supervisor Gregor Ahn.

Claudius Buchanan (1766–1815) worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Glasgow (1782) and Queens' College, Cambridge (~1791–1795), later serving as Vice-Provost at Fort William College (1801).

Claus Oetke (1947–2019) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (~1968–1976). He worked as a wissenschaftlicher Assistent at Hamburg (~1977–1989) and held a post at Stockholm University (~1989–2012).
Claus Vogel (1933–2012) was a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1964–1969), the University of Marburg (~1969–1976), and the University of Bonn (1976).

Colette Caillat (1921–2007) worked in Indology and linguistics. She served as Director at the University of Paris (~1972–1989) and held posts at the Institut de France and Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (~1979–2007).

Colette Sciberras is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at Durham University under David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, as well as under traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean works in philosophy and Indology, having studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria (attested 2002).

Collett Cox is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Columbia University under Alex Wayman and Yoshito S. Hakeda, and studied at Tokyo and Ryukoku universities. Cox held a professorship at the University of Washington (attested 1999–2017).
Conor Roddy is a philosophy scholar who completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2011) and studied under Arindam Chakrabarti and Roger T. Ames.

Constance E. Kassor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Smith College (BA) and Emory University (PhD, attested 2014) under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, later serving on the faculty at Smith College (attested 2014).

Constance Powell Chin specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed a Master's degree at San Jose State University in 2012 under John W. Bernhardt, and also studied under Christian Luczanits.

Constantin Regamey (1907–1982) worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, studying at Warsaw (~1927–1931) and Paris (~1932–1936). He held posts at the University of Warsaw (~1936–1941) and as professor at the universities of Lausanne (~1945–1977) and Fribourg (~1946–1977).

Cornelis Jan Kuiken specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Kuiken earned a PhD at the University of Groningen in 2002 under Timothy H. Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer, having also studied under Jaap den Hollander.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele (1830–1902) worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1848–1853) and served as Professor of the History of Religions at Leiden University (~1877–1901).
